method_notes: Weighted R32 performance and group stage form heavily, with secondary consideration for historical knockout pedigree and squad depth. Penalty shootout wins in R32 (Paraguay, Morocco, Egypt) noted as a mild fatigue and luck factor going into this round.

predictions.reasoning: France were the tournament's most dominant group-stage side and thrashed Sweden 3-0 in R32; Paraguay needed penalties to survive Germany and are significantly outclassed here.
Canada have been clinical and defensively solid; Morocco needed penalties to beat Netherlands and carry some fatigue, though their defensive organisation makes this close.
Brazil were imperious in the group stage and beat Japan comfortably; Norway's goals were largely accumulated against weaker sides and Brazil's quality is a clear level above.
England topped Group L convincingly and have the squad depth for a deep run; Mexico won their group but face a significant step up in class here.
Spain's group stage was flawless and their 3-0 win over Austria showed real authority; Portugal finished second in Group K and historically struggle against Spain's pressing system.
USA were solid throughout and benefit from home crowd advantage; Belgium showed defensive vulnerability in edging Senegal 3-2 and USA's pace in transition can exploit that.
Argentina were the only side with a perfect nine points and have Argentina's formidable knockout pedigree; Egypt reached this stage via penalties and are significantly outgunned.
Colombia topped Group K with the best defensive record in the tournament and beat Ghana efficiently; Switzerland are well-organised but Colombia's attacking variety gives them the edge.
